4:T74b,实验覆盖面比较完整，比较对象有 13 个公开 tokenizer，跨 48K 到 262K 四个词表规模、四类 pre-tokenizer。核心结果有几组。

1. 在 2700 万文档、28.4 亿词、46.21GB 的 Indic 预训练语料上，BrahmicTokenizer-131K 相比同为 131K 词表的 Tekken/Sarvam-m 总 token 数减少 26.7%。如果训练语料以 Indic 为主，这几乎可以直接理解成每步训练 compute 下降约 27%。

2. 优势覆盖 11/11 个 Brahmic 语言，幅度从 Tamil 的 15.79% 到 Odia 的 76.79%。Odia 是最能说明结构问题的例子：作者给出单句示例，37 个字符被 BrahmicTokenizer 切成 21 token，而 Tekken/Sarvam-m 切成 99 token；在 6030 万词的 Odia 子语料上，这种差距仍有 4.31 倍。原因也被直接验证：Tekken/Sarvam-m 的 131K 词表里没有 Oriya Unicode block token，于是每个字符基本都退化成 3 个 byte token。

3. 英文压缩几乎保持不变。FLORES-200 English 上是 1.235 tokens/word，o200k_base 是 1.232，Tekken/Sarvam-m 是 1.267。对 1000 篇英文文档，和 o200k_cropped 在 96.8% 文档上 tokenization 完全一致，总 token 数差异只有 0.034%。这说明 retrofit 的扰动确实很小。

4. 代码和数学压缩表现很好。HumanEval、MBPP、GSM8K 上分别达到 0.295、0.320、0.301 tokens/character。相对 Tekken/Sarvam-m 分别好 4.0%、5.4%、14.2%；相对词表规模是其两倍的 Sarvam-30B tokenizer，也仍然领先 13.2%、21.3%、16.6%。作者特别指出 GSM8K 的优势与 o200k_base 保留下来的单数字 tokenization 有关，这个细节对 reasoning/coding 预训练很重要。

5. 欧洲语言压缩基本维持竞争力。摘要截断处没有给完全部数字，但文中给出法语 1.464、德语 1.653、西语 1.388 tokens/word，说明裁剪和 retrofit 没有明显伤到这些高资源语言。5:T50a,The method has two stages. Stage one is a script-prune crop: starting from the 200,019-token o200k_base vocabulary, the authors reduce it to 131,072 tokens by removing 38,345 tokens associated with nine out-of-scope writing systems, while keeping the useful English/EU/code/math behavior inherited from o200k_base. Stage two is a surgical retrofit: within the cropped vocabulary, they identify 2,372 corpus-dead slots, meaning vocabulary entries that are effectively unused on the target corpus, and reassign those slots to high-frequency Brahmic content using a linear-programming allocation across nine Brahmic Unicode blocks.

The key design choice is what they do not change. The pre-tokenizer, decoder, and inherited merge rules remain untouched. This makes the tokenizer a drop-in replacement at the interface level and preserves much of the original segmentation behavior for English and code. The trade-off is clear: by not relearning merges, they give up some freedom to globally optimize Indic segmentation, but they gain compatibility and sharply reduce the risk of hurting strong existing domains. The LP-based slot allocation is also important: vocabulary budget is treated as a scarce resource that should be distributed according to corpus utility, not evenly across scripts.6:T740,The evaluation is fairly broad: 13 public tokenizers, four vocabulary classes from 48K to 262K, and four pre-tokenizer types. The main results are as follows.

1. On a 27M-document Indic pretraining corpus with 2.84B words and 46.21GB of text, BrahmicTokenizer-131K produces 26.7% fewer tokens than Tekken/Sarvam-m, which has the same 131K vocabulary budget. For Indic-heavy pretraining, that is close to a 27% reduction in per-step compute.

2. The gain holds for all 11 Brahmic languages, ranging from 15.79% on Tamil to 76.79% on Odia. Odia is the clearest structural case: a 37-character sentence becomes 21 tokens with the proposed tokenizer but 99 tokens with Tekken/Sarvam-m, and the same pattern persists at corpus scale with a 4.31x ratio on a 60.3M-word Odia subset. The reason is directly verifiable from the vocabulary: Tekken/Sarvam-m contains zero tokens from the Oriya Unicode block, so characters collapse to byte fallback.

3. English compression is nearly unchanged. On FLORES-200 English, the tokenizer gets 1.235 tokens/word versus 1.232 for o200k_base and 1.267 for Tekken/Sarvam-m. On 1,000 English documents, tokenization is byte-identical to o200k_cropped on 96.8% of documents, and the total token-count difference is only 0.034%.

4. Code and math compression remain strong. The tokenizer achieves 0.295, 0.320, and 0.301 tokens/character on HumanEval, MBPP, and GSM8K. Compared with Tekken/Sarvam-m, it is better by 4.0%, 5.4%, and 14.2%. It also beats the much larger-vocabulary Sarvam-30B tokenizer by 13.2%, 21.3%, and 16.6% on the same three sets. The GSM8K gain is tied to preserving o200k_base’s digit tokenization behavior, which is relevant for reasoning and code pretraining.

5. European-language compression stays competitive, with reported FLORES values of 1.464 for French, 1.653 for German, and 1.388 for Spanish.7:T49e,For a quick but useful read, focus on three parts.

Two follow-up questions are worth thinking about: how corpus-dependent the notion of dead slots is, and how far this retrofit strategy can scale if one wants to cover other underrepresented scripts without changing merge rules.8:T9a2,KletterMix 的核心思路是把一个现成的高质量英语 mixture ClimbMix 翻译成德语，并尽量保持 mixture-level 设计不变。方法上有几个关键点。

第一，保留 document boundary 和 metadata。每条记录不仅有翻译后的德语文本，还保留原始 document id、source cluster、source location、近似长度等字段，并额外记录翻译过程元数据，如 context bucket、chunking 状态、translation config、quality estimation 输出。这样做的意义很直接：后续可以按 source cluster 做质量分析、长度比分析、topic coverage 对齐，也可以在训练时做更细的 mixture 控制。

第二，length-aware routing。预训练语料的文档长度分布很长尾，直接统一翻译会在长文档上出现截断、预算不足、上下文溢出和质量退化。作者因此按长度和上下文需求做路由，对超长文档采用 chunking，同时尽量维持文档级组织，而不是退化成句子级翻译。这里的取舍很重要：如果完全按句子切分，翻译更稳，但会破坏预训练语料的篇章结构；如果强行整篇翻译，长文档质量和吞吐都会出问题。KletterMix 选择的是文档优先、必要时分块。

第三，scalable shard-wise execution。源语料本身是 sharded JSONL，翻译流程按 shard 执行，便于大规模并行处理、失败恢复和一致性检查。这更像真正面向数百亿到数千亿 token 数据工程的设计，而不是实验室级小规模翻译。

第四，post-hoc quality estimation。作者使用 COMETKiwi 作为 reference-free 质量估计信号，并进一步训练 target-only proxy model 做 corpus-level 质量估计。这个设计很有意思，因为大规模预训练语料不可能逐条人工验收，而仅靠翻译模型自信度也不够。COMETKiwi 提供较强的外部 QE 信号，但推理成本高；target-only proxy 则更适合大规模筛选和后续复用。论文还结合长度分布、source composition、topic coverage、metadata preservation 做多维诊断，避免只用单一 QE 分数判断语料质量。

第五，数据集变体与 annealing 评估。作者不仅发布一个总语料，还考察 proxy filtering、不同语料混合和 annealing 场景，说明他们关心的不只是“翻出来多少 token”，而是这些 token 在训练流程中的最佳使用方式。对预训练研究者来说，这一点比单纯语料规模更重要。9:T915,KletterMix is built by translating ClimbMix, a strong English pretraining mixture, into German while preserving the original mixture design as much as possible. Several design choices are central.

First, document boundaries and metadata are preserved. Each translated record keeps the original document ID, source cluster, source location, and approximate length, and adds processing metadata such as context bucket, chunking status, translation configuration, and quality-estimation outputs. This is important because it keeps the corpus analyzable at the source level rather than collapsing it into anonymous text.

Second, the pipeline uses length-aware routing. Pretraining corpora have a heavy-tailed document-length distribution, so naive translation would cause truncation, context overflow, and quality degradation on long documents. The pipeline therefore routes documents by length and context needs, and applies chunking only when necessary, while still prioritizing document-level preservation. This is a deliberate trade-off: sentence-level translation would be easier and often cleaner, but it would destroy discourse structure that matters for language modeling.

Third, translation is executed shard-wise at scale. Since the source corpus is stored as sharded JSONL, the pipeline processes shards independently, which supports large-scale parallelism, fault recovery, and consistency checks. This is the kind of systems choice that matters when the target corpus is hundreds of billions of tokens.

Fourth, the paper adds post-hoc quality estimation. It uses COMETKiwi as a reference-free quality-estimation signal and also trains a target-only proxy model for corpus-level quality estimation. This is a practical combination: COMETKiwi provides a stronger but more expensive signal, while the proxy model is more scalable for filtering and repeated use. The corpus is further analyzed through length distributions, source composition, topic coverage, and metadata preservation, instead of relying on a single QE score.

Fifth, the work studies dataset variants and annealing settings rather than releasing only one monolithic corpus. That makes the paper more relevant to actual pretraining workflows, where the question is not only how much data exists, but how it should be filtered, mixed, and scheduled.a:T5fa,The core empirical claim is established through controlled pretraining and annealing comparisons against existing German corpora. The headline scale is clear from the paper: KletterMix contains about 725B German tokens, which makes it large enough to matter as a standalone pretraining or annealing resource rather than a small auxiliary dataset.

First, direct comparisons against established German-data baselines under controlled pretraining or annealing setups, measuring downstream German-language performance. The contribution is ecosystem instrumentation and partner governance, not a model-training technique.f:Ta76,架构上，Mellum 2 是 decoder-only Transformer，基本沿用 Qwen3-MoE 路线：每层都有 MoE FFN，64 experts、8 active experts，配 GQA、QK-Norm、SiLU-gated MLP、RMSNorm、RoPE。作者的目标不是追求最大参数，而是在单 H100 上把延迟压到接近 Qwen2.5-7B，因此做了三项偏部署导向的修改。

第一是 GQA 且只保留 4 个 KV heads。报告明确指出，在高并发场景下，KV heads 数量是吞吐的关键瓶颈之一；同步单请求时影响不大，但真实服务下会直接决定 KV cache 带宽和显存压力。第二是 Sliding Window Attention，只在四分之三的层上启用，用局部注意力换取更低推理成本，同时保留部分全局层维持跨段信息流。第三是单个 MTP head，既作为预训练辅助目标，也作为 speculative decoding 的内置 draft head。这一点比较实用：训练时增加 next-multiple-token 的学习信号，推理时直接复用为草稿模型，减少额外 draft model 的部署复杂度。

作者系统比较了 dense、MoE 和 MLA 路线。结论是：在给定延迟预算下，dense 配置即便调整层数和宽度，也难稳定超过 Qwen2.5-7B；MLA 虽然能在等速下把参数做大到约 5.5B，但质量收益不足以覆盖训练复杂度，而且适合该尺度的 latent rank 不理想。因此最终选择 MoE，把总参数扩到约 12B，同时把每 token 计算维持在 2.5B dense 左右。

训练上采用三阶段预训练 curriculum，总计约 10.6T token，遵循“web early, curated late”思路，代码占比从 23% 提升到 42%，再到 59%，同时 batch size 翻倍，并在最后加入 capability-sharpening phase，把学习率线性衰减到 0。这个设计反映了一个明确判断：前期需要更广覆盖的数据维持通用性，后期再提高代码和数学密度去打磨目标能力，而不是一开始就用高纯度代码语料。优化器用 Muon，训练精度用 FP8 hybrid mixed precision，学习率调度是 Warmup-Hold-Decay 并线性降到 0。报告强调他们在十万亿 token 级别的 MoE 训练中观察了稳定性问题，这部分如果写得细，会比常见技术报告更有价值。

长上下文扩展阶段，把预训练 base 扩到 131,072 token，采用 Gemma 3 / OLMo 3 风格的 layer-selective scaling，并用 YaRN 做 RoPE scaling。这里的重点不是单纯把 context 拉长，而是观察数据混合在长上下文继续训练中的迁移，以及 MoE router 在这一阶段的行为变化。后训练则从同一个 long-context checkpoint 分出 Instruct 和 Thinking 两个版本，并用 RLVR 在数学和可执行代码任务上继续强化。10:T9d6,Mellum 2 is a decoder-only Transformer built on a Qwen3-MoE-style backbone: MoE feed-forward blocks in every layer, 64 experts with 8 active per token, GQA, QK-Norm, SiLU-gated MLPs, RMSNorm, and RoPE. The model has about 12B total parameters with 2.5B active parameters per token.

Three deployment-oriented modifications define the design. First, it uses GQA with only 4 KV heads. The report explicitly argues that KV-head count is a major throughput bottleneck under high concurrency because it directly affects KV-cache bandwidth and memory pressure. Second, it applies Sliding Window Attention to three out of every four layers, reducing attention cost while preserving some global-attention layers for long-range information flow. Third, it adds a single Multi-Token Prediction head. This head serves two roles: an auxiliary pretraining objective and an internal draft head for speculative decoding. That is a practical systems choice, because it improves training signal density and inference efficiency without requiring a separate draft model.

The architecture search compares dense backbones, MoE variants, GQA settings, MLA, SWA patterns, and sparsity ratios. The conclusion is straightforward: under the target latency budget, dense models do not consistently beat a Qwen2.5-7B baseline; MLA allows somewhat larger dense-equivalent models but does not justify the added complexity at this scale; MoE is the only route that meaningfully expands total parameter capacity while keeping per-token compute low enough for deployment.

Pretraining follows a three-phase curriculum over roughly 10.6T tokens. The data mix shifts from broad web-heavy data to more curated code and math, with code ratio increasing from 23% to 42% to 59%. Batch size doubles across phases, and the final stage uses an extended capability-sharpening phase with linear decay of the learning rate to zero. The optimizer is Muon, training uses hybrid FP8 mixed precision, and the LR schedule is Warmup-Hold-Decay. The report frames this as a production-scale MoE recipe rather than a one-off experiment.

For long-context extension, the pretrained base is continued to 131,072 tokens using a layer-selective scaling recipe similar to Gemma 3 and OLMo 3, with YaRN for positional scaling. The report also mentions empirical observations on data-mixture transfer and MoE router dynamics during this stage. Post-training then branches into Instruct and Thinking variants, both further refined with RLVR on math and executable coding tasks.11:T693,The key configuration is 12B total parameters, 2.5B active parameters per token, 64 experts with 8 active, about 10.6T pretraining tokens, and a 128K context extension. The report claims throughput matching or exceeding Qwen2.5-7B on a single H100 while remaining competitive with open-weight models in the 4–14B range on code, math, reasoning, tool use, knowledge, and safety benchmarks.

The most informative experiments are the architecture ablations. One explicit result is that using 2 active experts gives about 1.5x lower latency than using 8 active experts, but quality drops enough that 8/64 is chosen as the better quality-latency trade-off. The report also states that under the same latency budget, MoE can scale total parameter count into roughly the 15B feasible region, whereas dense alternatives cannot deliver the same knowledge capacity.

Serving-oriented measurements are another important part. The report highlights KV-head count as the dominant factor for high-concurrency throughput, which makes the 4-KV-head design a systems-driven choice rather than a cosmetic tweak. If the full report includes throughput curves across concurrency regimes, those are worth close attention.

The training and long-context sections appear to contain observations on Muon+FP8 stability at MoE scale, as well as router behavior during 128K extension. Even without all numbers in the provided excerpt, these analyses are likely more useful than the headline benchmark scores. A careful reader should look for loss stability, load balancing, short-context regression after long-context extension, and ablations isolating the contribution of MTP to both training and inference.12:T46a,Its main contribution is conceptual before it is architectural. The paper connects representation degeneration and anisotropy to the pre-training objective itself, not merely to post hoc embedding analysis. If that diagnosis is correct, then objective design for LLM pre-training is missing an important ingredient: explicit supervision over latent structure. The proposed fix is also restrained in a useful way. It does not replace the Transformer, does not introduce a separate encoder, and does not require expensive distillation. Instead, it augments NTP with a self-generated continuous target from the model’s own shallow layers. That makes NITP relevant as a lightweight objective regularizer rather than a new end-to-end training stack. For pre-training research, the paper suggests three broader directions: token likelihood alone may be insufficient to shape robust internal representations; shallow/deep layer specialization can be exploited as a self-supervised signal; and comparisons across language modeling paradigms should pay more attention to representation geometry, not only perplexity or downstream scores.13:T8b3,The method is simple in form but carefully chosen in its details. In a standard causal LM, the final hidden state h_t at position t is used to predict token x_{t+1}. NITP adds an auxiliary objective that asks h_t to predict an implicit representation of the next token. This implicit token is not the vocabulary embedding and not a feature from an external teacher. It is the hidden state of the same model at position t+1 from a shallow layer, denoted as a latent target with stop-gradient applied. Training jointly optimizes the usual cross-entropy for NTP and a cosine-similarity-style loss between h_t and the shallow representation of x_{t+1}.

Several design choices matter. First, why use a shallow-layer target instead of a deep-layer target? The paper argues that shallow layers preserve richer lexical and local semantic information, while deeper layers are more task-specialized and may already reflect the geometric degeneration induced by NTP. Using shallow states therefore provides a denser and less collapsed target. Second, why predict the representation at t+1 rather than reconstruct the current token? Because the auxiliary task is meant to stay aligned with the causal next-token objective and preserve the autoregressive temporal structure. Third, why use a continuous latent target rather than label smoothing or another output-space modification? Because output-space tweaks still supervise the model mainly through logits, whereas NITP directly constrains the hidden representation.

The theoretical framing is that gradients under NTP are dominated by the correct token and a few strong competitors, so optimization mainly constrains h_t along directions tied to those embeddings. A large orthogonal subspace remains nearly loss-invariant. This creates a broad but weakly constrained landscape in which geometrically poor hidden states can achieve similar token likelihood. NITP reduces that freedom by adding dense vector-level supervision, effectively anchoring hidden states in representation space. Implementation cost is low because the target features are already produced in the same forward pass; the extra overhead is mostly the auxiliary similarity loss and any small alignment head if used.14:T886,The experimental story is centered on validating the paper’s diagnosis rather than merely reporting benchmark gains. The first and most important set of results tracks representation geometry during training. The authors monitor Effective Rank and average cosine similarity among token representations in a batch. Under standard NTP, effective rank drops quickly while cosine similarity rises, indicating that representations collapse into a narrower and more anisotropic subspace. With NITP, effective rank stays higher and anisotropy grows more slowly. This is the key evidence that the method is acting on the mechanism it claims to address.

The second set of results concerns downstream or generalization performance. The abstract states that NITP consistently improves downstream results, and the introduction frames the gains as stable rather than isolated. The full numerical tables are not present in the provided excerpt, so it would be unsafe to invent exact model sizes, token counts, or deltas. The paper formulates one epoch of training as a discrete dynamical system over parameters. The dataset is partitioned into train-units, either at the sample level or batch level. Because gradient updates do not commute in a non-convex landscape, the final parameter state depends on the order of train-units, so scheduling becomes a combinatorial optimization problem over permutations.

The key idea is a dynamic influence graph. A directed edge from i to j represents whether training on i now is expected to reduce the future loss on j. This is defined through look-ahead loss reduction, with a parameter gamma controlling the temporal scale of the interaction: smaller gamma captures more local effects, while larger gamma approximates longer-range influence. This is the main conceptual move of the paper. Instead of asking whether a sample is intrinsically good or hard, the method asks whether it prepares the model for later data.

The schedule is then derived as the solution to an optimization problem constrained by this graph structure, so the training sequence respects the learned directional dependencies. The paper also mentions scalable approximations for graph construction and solving, aimed at making the method practical in large-scale settings. From the provided excerpt, however, the exact approximation quality, computational complexity, and update frequency still need to be checked in the later methodology and experiments.17:T611,SMET has three main components. The first is optimizer-state warm-up for regrown parameters. When a connection is activated, its weight may be initialized reasonably, but its Adam moments are effectively newborn. Applying the same optimizer rule as for mature parameters creates a cold-start problem: the update magnitude and direction are not calibrated by historical statistics. SMET introduces a controlled warm-up phase so that newly activated weights do not inject abrupt disturbances into training immediately after topology changes. The second component is density-aware learning-rate scaling. Warm-up improves stability but also makes updates more conservative. In sparse regimes, the effective parameterization and gradient statistics differ from dense training, so simply reusing the dense learning-rate recipe slows progress. The density-aware scaling compensates for this and better matches optimization to the active parameter budget. The third component is a memory-efficient sparse optimizer implementation. Instead of keeping dense tensors plus binary masks, SMET stores gradients and optimizer states only for active parameters. This is important because many sparse-training implementations save parameters sparsely but still pay dense-state memory costs. The method supports both unstructured and block sparsity, which matters for eventual practicality. - Layer/interpolation analyses indicate middle-layer drift is the main driver for comprehension degradation, while translation exhibits a different layer sensitivity profile—implying no single “protect the middle” rule fits all objectives.1c:T73e,The core construction is group averaging. If the loss is invariant under a parameter transformation group G, then the gradient transforms equivariantly under the same group action. Starting from a single gradient at one parameter point, the method analytically averages gradient-derived quantities over the group orbit and uses that average as a proxy for local curvature. The resulting Hessian approximation is guaranteed to lie in the commutant algebra of the group representation. This is the key structural result: instead of storing a dense curvature matrix, one only needs coefficients over a small basis of symmetry-compatible operators.

The paper then instantiates this idea for MLPs and Transformers. For each architecture, the complexity of the approximation is tied to the dimension of the commutant algebra induced by the selected symmetry group. Large groups impose stronger constraints, giving cheaper and more compact approximations, but their orbits are less local and may wash out true local curvature. Smaller groups preserve more local information but increase computational burden. This is presented as an explicit design knob rather than a side effect.

A practical contribution is a just-in-time compiler that takes symbolic symmetry specifications and emits efficient PyTorch routines for computing the low-dimensional factors. So the framework is not only an abstract characterization; it is meant to be operational.

A major theoretical bridge is the derivation showing that particular permutation subgroup choices recover Shampoo/Muon-like curvature structures. This is important because it turns those optimizers from isolated engineering designs into points inside a broader symmetry-aware family. In other words, Kronecker/block structure is not merely a computational convenience here; it emerges from symmetry constraints.1d:T4b0,From the provided full text, the experimental agenda is centered on validation rather than large-scale language-model pretraining wins. A quick skim takes around 40 minutes; a serious read with proofs and Transformer sections is closer to 1.5–2 hours.1f:T55c,The hyper-epoch pretraining (q0) framework consists of three core primitives:

1. **Cyclic Parallel Schedule**: Inspired by Fast Geometric Ensembling (FGE), short training cycles with anti-correlated learning rate and weight decay (LR rises as WD falls and vice versa) collect many model snapshots along a small number of parallel trajectories. Only a few trajectories are trained from scratch with different random initializations; the rest are generated through cyclic exploration, dramatically reducing exploration cost.

2. **Chain Distillation**: Each new snapshot is trained against its predecessor as a teacher, in addition to the standard objective. This allows the population's capability to compound across training, rather than producing models of similar individual quality as in traditional ensembling.

3. **Learned Weighting at Inference**: Weights for each model are learned on a held-out fitness set, replacing simple uniform averaging. The weight assignment exhibits non-trivial behavior: snapshots that are not individually optimal under validation loss but complementary for ensembling receive substantial weight.

Key differences from traditional ensembling: naive ensembling trains every model from scratch (wastes compute), produces models of homogeneous quality, and uses uniform weighting (ignoring individual differences). q0 addresses all three.20:T424,The paper explains two tightly coupled questions in Muon: why momentum is empirically indispensable, and why it must be applied before orthogonalization rather than after it. Prior analyses typically isolated the polar update and removed momentum, or kept momentum only in convergence proofs that did not explain its practical benefit. That leaves a gap between theory and LLM pretraining practice, where standard Muon clearly outperforms both a no-momentum variant and an orthogonalize-first variant. The paper argues that the key role of momentum in Muon is not generic acceleration. It is spectral filtering on the matrix gradient stream. Momentum suppresses temporally incoherent perturbations while preserving persistent low-rank signal, thereby enlarging the singular-value gap and stabilizing the leading singular subspaces. Orthogonalization should then act on this denoised matrix. If polar normalization is applied first, it destroys the amplitude information that separates signal from noise, and later momentum cannot recover that lost distinction.21:T78d,The technical setup combines a structured gradient model with a comparison of three update pipelines. Gradients are modeled as a coherent low-rank signal plus a bounded-variance, mean-zero perturbation that is orthogonal to the signal. This is a deliberate abstraction: it captures the idea that some directions persist across steps and should accumulate, while other components behave like high-frequency noise.

The paper studies three pipelines. Pre-polar is standard Muon: first form the momentum buffer M_t = beta M_{t-1} + (1-beta) G_t, then apply the polar factor O(M_t). Post-polar is the Orthogonal-SGDM style variant: first orthogonalize each step O(G_t), then apply momentum. Polar-only removes momentum entirely. The first main result is that momentum acts as a spectral low-pass filter on the raw gradient stream. Because the coherent signal persists over time, it survives temporal averaging; the zero-mean perturbation is attenuated. This enlarges the gap between the r-th and (r+1)-th singular values and improves alignment of the top-r singular subspaces of M_t with those of the underlying signal. The second main result is about ordering. The polar factor preserves singular directions but replaces singular values by ones. If it is applied directly to a noisy gradient, it erases the magnitude structure that distinguishes signal from perturbation. Momentum applied afterward can only smooth already distorted directions; it cannot recreate the lost spectral separation. Hence pre-polar dominates post-polar for structural reasons, not as an implementation accident.

A useful aspect of the analysis is that it does not stop at the vague statement “momentum reduces noise.” It specifies what kind of noise reduction matters for Muon: creating a matrix whose spectrum is sufficiently separated so that the subsequent orthogonalization acts on stable leading subspaces. That is the optimizer-specific mechanism.22:T615,The experimental goal is to validate the spectral-filtering story and the ordering effect, rather than to introduce a new benchmark result. The paper first compares pre-polar, post-polar, and polar-only in pretraining. The qualitative result is clear from the introduction: standard pre-polar Muon consistently outperforms both alternatives throughout training, showing that momentum is essential and that the order cannot be swapped.

The more informative experiments are the spectral diagnostics. The theory predicts that the momentum buffer should exhibit a larger top-r versus tail singular-value separation than the raw gradient, and that the leading singular subspaces should align better with the coherent signal. It also predicts that post-polar loses this advantage because orthogonalizing G_t first flattens all singular values to one. The full paper likely includes plots of spectral gap versus momentum strength or effective window size, subspace alignment metrics, and update-direction comparisons under controlled signal-plus-noise settings. If reading for a quick mechanism check, the introduction, main theorems, and the spectral diagnostic figures should be enough in about an hour.24:T5a9,The method, FINEVERIFY, has a proposer-verifier structure. A proposer first runs agentic search and samples multiple trajectories, producing a set of candidate answers. The verifier does not assign one global score per candidate. Instead, it first decomposes the original question into a set of checkable sub-questions, each corresponding to a requirement, attribute, or constraint in the task. Then, for every candidate answer, it verifies each sub-question against retrieved evidence and labels the result as supported, not_found, or contradicted. These per-check judgments are aggregated into an evidence-grounded verification score, and the highest-scoring candidate is selected.

Relative to best-of-N or confidence-based reranking, the design changes the problem in three ways. First, it replaces one difficult global judgment with multiple simpler local judgments. Second, all candidates are evaluated against the same explicit checklist, which makes scores more comparable across candidates. Third, the aggregation rule is explicit rather than implicit, so the final decision is inspectable.

The paper also uses a practical early-stopping rule: if a candidate receives full support on all sub-questions, sampling can stop because further compute is unlikely to change the decision. Another useful byproduct is the verification trace itself, which can be used to audit benchmark quality and diagnose why a candidate was accepted or rejected.25:T57f,The evaluation covers four agentic search benchmarks and two models. It consistently beats standard test-time scaling baselines such as Majority Voting, Weighted Voting, Best-of-N, Solution Aggregation, and Confidence Verify.

The more important result is that it keeps improving as the number of samples grows. 全文最关键的技术判断是：self-verification 比 likelihood 派生分数更适合作为无监督 correctness score。原因有三。第一，它条件在完整候选答案上，而不是只看生成概率，因此更接近后验判断。第二，它和下游目标语义一致，问的是“这个答案对不对”，而不是“这个答案像不像模型平时会说的话”。第三，作者把它定义为 verdict token 的归一化概率 s_sv = p(✓)/(p(✓)+p(✗))，从而减少绝对 logit 尺度带来的不稳定。

另一个有意思的点是 virtual thinking prefix。作者在 self-verification 判别前插入一串不对用户可见的 filler tokens，让模型多消耗一些计算，再读取最后的 verdict logits。这里不是让模型生成完整 reasoning，而只是让 verifier 侧做一个二分类判断。作者发现结构化 filler，比如倒计时 token，比简单的点号更有效。这个观察和一些 prior work 中“无训练 filler token 对生成侧 reasoning 没用”的结论不同。作者给出的解释是，verifier-side 的任务更简单，只需把内部状态推到更可分的 verdict，而不需要维持长程连贯文本生成。

方法上的另一贡献是把 score quality、decoding effectiveness、aggregation effectiveness 分开评估。也就是说，某个分数本身排序能力强，不代表它与某种 decoder 结合后就一定带来更高准确率。全文反复强调 score 的好坏不是静态属性，而是由 decoder 如何消费它共同决定。这一点在分析 SMC/MCMC 时尤其重要，因为分数动态范围不合适会导致粒子塌缩或采样退化。28:T8b5,The main contribution is a unified score × decoder grid. On the score side, the paper compares four intrinsic signals: perplexity, contrastive scoring, power-distribution likelihood, and self-verification. On the decoder side, it compares three families that consume those scores: optimization, sampling, and consensus. Optimization is instantiated as best-of-N. Sampling is implemented with SMC and MCMC over a reweighted target distribution p_final(y|x) ∝ p_LM(y|x) · s(y|x). Consensus selects the modal answer under that induced distribution, using either majority vote or score-weighted aggregation.

The central technical claim is that self-verification is structurally better suited than likelihood-derived scores for unsupervised elicitation. It conditions on the full candidate answer, is semantically aligned with the downstream objective, and is defined as a normalized verdict probability, s_sv = p(check)/(p(check)+p(cross)). That normalization reduces sensitivity to absolute logit scale and makes the score more comparable across candidates.

A second notable idea is the virtual-thinking prefix. Before producing the final verification verdict, the model is forced to consume a sequence of filler tokens that spend extra compute without exposing visible reasoning. The paper finds that structured fillers, such as countdown tokens, work better than uniform fillers like repeated dots. This is an interesting contrast with prior work showing that plug-and-play filler tokens are ineffective for generator-side latent reasoning without training. The authors’ explanation is plausible: verifier-side virtual thinking is an easier task because the model only needs to sharpen a binary judgment, not generate a coherent reasoning trace.

Another strong aspect of the paper is the evaluation design. It separates score quality, decoding effectiveness, and aggregation effectiveness. A score that ranks candidates well in a fixed pool does not necessarily improve best-of-N or sampling-based decoding. The paper repeatedly shows that score quality is not an intrinsic scalar property; it depends on how the decoder consumes the score, especially when dynamic-range mismatch or particle collapse appears in SMC/MCMC.29:T5d2,Experiments are run on MATH500 using both the base and instruction-tuned Qwen3-1.7B. Importantly, the paper evaluates the full score × decoder grid rather than highlighting only one favorable combination. The broad result is that self-verification with virtual thinking performs best or near-best on many axes, especially for candidate ranking and unsupervised selection, but no single score dominates every decoder and every metric. That restraint makes the empirical story more credible.

The evaluation has three layers. First, score quality: with a fixed candidate pool, can the score rank correct answers above incorrect ones, measured by per-question AUROC and top-k accuracy. Second, decoding effectiveness: once the score is plugged into best-of-N, SMC, or MCMC, does it improve single-answer accuracy over vanilla decoding. Third, aggregation effectiveness: when many samples are available, does score-weighted consensus beat majority vote or simple best-of-N selection.

- Actions: discrete choices—stop (return current majority vote) or sample k_l additional candidates in parallel.

- Policy: a small 4-layer MLP trained with RL; runs on CPU; wraps around any black-box LLM sampler.
- Design trade-off: using only answer-level statistics improves portability and operational simplicity, but forgoes stronger internal signals (logits, token-level uncertainty, process features), which may cap achievable efficiency gains.2c:Ta77,方法分两阶段。第一阶段是 empirical law discovery。作者先在小规模 proxy 模型上系统扫描不同 compute budget、学习率和 batch size，观察在 continued pre-training 过程中最优超参如何随训练推进而变化。全文给出的主要经验规律是：随着可用 compute 增加，最优 batch size 单调增大，而最优 learning rate 相应减小。这里的“相应”不是口头描述，而是通过标准 loss-compute scaling 关系推导出从 compute 到最优超参的函数映射。也就是说，作者不是直接拟合“步数→超参”，而是先把训练轨迹放到 compute/loss 坐标里，再建立超参最优点的函数形式。这个设计的好处是更容易跨模型规模和训练阶段迁移。

第二阶段是 quantifying the initial optimization state，也就是论文最关键的 equivalent pre-training compute。作者认为，一个任意 checkpoint 虽然来自别的预训练分布，但仍可以在目标域上通过 validation loss 定位到一条连续训练轨迹上的某个坐标。具体做法是：先在目标域上建立 loss 与 compute 的对应关系，再把 checkpoint 当前的 target-domain validation loss 映射成一个等效的已投入算力 C_pre。之后，把计划中的 continued pre-training 算力 C_cpt 加上去，得到总有效算力 C_total = C_pre + C_cpt。最后，把 C_total 代入第一阶段得到的超参标度律，直接预测该 run 的最优学习率和 batch size。

这个框架和传统做法的区别有三点。其一，传统 recipe 往往只看模型参数量、token 数或经验 warmup 规则，而这里显式把“checkpoint 当前状态”作为一等公民。其二，传统超参迁移通常依赖同架构、同数据、相近训练阶段的经验复用；这里试图用 loss-based coordinate 把不同生命周期的 checkpoint 放到统一坐标系。其三，很多 CPT 调参默认先固定 batch 再找 LR，或者反过来分步搜索；这篇工作把二者都写成 compute 的函数，目标是一次性 zero-shot 给出配置。

从全文表述看，这个方法隐含几个前提。一个前提是 target-domain loss 与有效 compute 之间存在足够平滑、可拟合的关系，否则 C_pre 的反演会不稳。另一个前提是 proxy 模型上发现的最优超参函数在更大模型和不同架构上保持形状稳定，只需做尺度迁移。论文声称 Dense 和 MoE 都验证了这一点，但阅读时需要特别留意：这种稳定性到底是“趋势一致”，还是参数化形式和系数都能可靠迁移。这里决定了方法是 recipe 级工具，还是只是一种较好的初始化器。2d:T8e2,The method has two stages.

Stage 1 is empirical law discovery. The authors train small proxy models under continued pre-training across a range of compute budgets and hyperparameter settings, then identify how the optimal learning rate and batch size evolve as training proceeds. The main empirical pattern reported in the paper is that the optimal batch size increases monotonically with compute budget, while the optimal learning rate decreases accordingly. Rather than fitting hyperparameters directly against steps, the framework uses standard loss-compute scaling relationships to derive mappings from compute to optimal hyperparameters. This is an important design choice because compute is a more transferable coordinate than raw step count when model size and setup vary.

Stage 2 is quantifying the initial optimization state. This is the key conceptual move. A checkpoint inherited from prior pre-training is treated as a point on a continuous target-domain training trajectory. The paper maps the checkpoint’s validation loss on the target domain to an equivalent amount of pre-training compute, denoted C_pre. Planned continued pre-training compute is C_cpt, and the total effective compute becomes C_total = C_pre + C_cpt. The optimal learning rate and batch size are then predicted zero-shot by plugging C_total into the scaling laws discovered in Stage 1.

Compared with standard practice, the framework differs in three ways. First, it explicitly models checkpoint state instead of relying on model size, token count, or inherited recipes alone. Second, it uses a loss-based coordinate system to place checkpoints from different lifecycle stages onto a common axis. Third, it aims to predict both LR and batch size jointly, instead of doing sequential search or fixing one while tuning the other.

The method does rely on nontrivial assumptions. The target-domain loss-to-compute curve must be smooth enough to invert reliably. The proxy-discovered hyperparameter laws must also transfer in shape across larger scales and different architectures. The paper claims this holds for both dense and MoE models, but the strength of that claim depends on whether only the trend transfers or the actual parameterized law remains accurate enough for zero-shot use.2e:T78f,The experimental story has three layers.

First, the paper needs to show that the scaling regularities actually exist. On proxy models, it reports that optimal batch size grows with compute while optimal learning rate decreases, and that these relationships are stable across scales. The key question when reading the figures is whether this is merely local monotonicity or a clean functional law over a broad compute range.

Second, the paper needs to validate equivalent pre-training compute. The central claim is that checkpoints from arbitrary prior states can be mapped to C_pre using target-domain validation loss, and that this quantity is sufficient to predict good hyperparameters for future CPT. The most informative comparisons are against heuristic recipes and explicit grid search, ideally across multiple starting checkpoints. If those experiments are present, they are more important than single-run wins because they test whether the framework really handles non-zero initialization rather than overfitting one setup.

Third, the paper needs to demonstrate scale transfer and practical savings. The abstract states validation up to Dense-8B and MoE-3B, with 70–90% lower tuning cost than grid search while improving stability and performance. When reading the full results, the important details are: how close the predicted hyperparameters are to the best searched configuration; whether gains are measured in validation loss, perplexity, or downstream metrics; what “improved stability” means in practice—fewer loss spikes, fewer divergences, smoother convergence; and whether the 70–90% saving counts only tuning overhead or the full training budget. The most important ablations are likely removing C_pre and predicting from C_cpt alone, or predicting only LR or only batch size. Those tests reveal whether equivalent compute is the real driver and whether both hyperparameters need to be modeled jointly.2f:T6bc,Read it in three passes: framing, state quantification, then scale transfer.

Start with the introduction and the overview figure to lock down the problem formulation. The paper is not about generic HPO and not about predicting final loss. It is about zero-shot prediction of optimal LR and batch size for a given checkpoint and CPT budget.

Then read carefully the section defining equivalent pre-training compute. This is the conceptual center of the paper. Focus on three questions: how the target-domain loss-to-compute mapping is fit, why that mapping remains meaningful under distribution shift, and what empirical evidence supports the additivity assumption C_total = C_pre + C_cpt. If these pieces are weak, the framework becomes a useful heuristic rather than a principled coordinate system.

Next, inspect the empirical law discovery figures and fitted equations. Check whether the LR and batch-size trends are only qualitative or whether they admit a stable functional form that transfers across model sizes and across dense versus MoE settings.

In the experiments, prioritize: zero-shot prediction versus grid search and heuristic baselines; transfer across different starting checkpoints; and the large-model validations on Dense-8B and MoE-3B. If time is limited, these are the sections to read before the full ablations.

Two deeper follow-up questions are worth keeping in mind. One is whether equivalent compute can survive larger recipe changes, such as tokenizer shifts, data-mixture changes, or post-train-to-pretrain feedback loops. The other is whether total effective compute is sufficient, or whether data difficulty, domain distance, or gradient-noise-scale variables need to be modeled explicitly.30:T5be,The method, CLAD, has three main components. First, it builds confidence-induced clusters (CICs). At a denoising step, the decoder computes token-level confidence for masked positions and merges adjacent high-confidence masked tokens into maximal contiguous spans. Each span becomes a candidate update unit. The underlying assumption is simple but important: neighboring confident positions are often supported by the same local context and can be committed together. Second, CLAD estimates dependencies between clusters. Instead of training an auxiliary module, it reuses self-attention maps from the same forward pass, aggregates token-level interactions into inter-cluster dependency scores, and constructs a conflict graph. To keep the graph sparse, it retains only mutually strongest inter-cluster dependencies. This pruning is important; otherwise the graph becomes too dense and the decoder turns overly conservative. Third, CLAD selects a maximum-weight set of non-conflicting clusters for parallel commitment. Cluster weights come from aggregated confidence. This turns each denoising step into a constrained combinatorial selection problem rather than independent token ranking. Relative to token-level dependency-aware methods such as DAPD and DAWN, the key difference is not merely using attention at cluster level. The deeper change is the two-stage decomposition: define locally reliable span candidates first, then resolve global compatibility among them.31:T4d7,The evaluation covers mathematical reasoning and code generation, using pretrained MDLMs from the LLaDA and Dream families on four benchmarks. The main result is a 1.77× to 8.47× speedup over vanilla decoding while keeping task accuracy broadly comparable in most settings. Against token-level dependency-aware baselines such as DAPD and DAWN, CLAD improves throughput in most evaluated cases. The reported gains appear to come from two sources: cluster-level commitment reduces the number of denoising iterations, and attention-based compatibility modeling limits the quality drop that would otherwise come from aggressively committing multiple spans at once. The key ablation to look for is the separation between the two ingredients: using CICs without conflict filtering should improve speed but hurt accuracy more, while token-level dependency modeling without cluster grouping should leave parallelism underexploited. The paper also stresses that sparsifying the conflict graph is necessary for efficiency; otherwise the overhead of cluster selection would eat into the decoding gains. The abstract does not provide finer benchmark-level numbers or sensitivity analyses, so those need to be checked in the main tables and appendix.32:T926,The core object is a generalized linear recurrence. For each position i, the output y_i is written as the sum of two terms: a linear combination of past inputs x_j with coefficients alpha_{i,j}, and a linear combination of past outputs y_j with coefficients beta_{i,j}. In matrix form, this becomes Y = AX + BY, hence Y = (I - B)^{-1}AX, where A is lower triangular and B is strictly lower triangular.

This formulation does several useful things. First, attention appears as the special case B = 0: all influence is direct input-to-output mixing, with no explicit recurrent propagation through previous outputs. RNN/SSM-like models correspond to structured B, often with banded or subdiagonal patterns, plus constrained A. That reduces architectural differences to the structure of A and B rather than to surface-level implementation categories.

Second, the paper isolates recurrence order as an independent design axis. Standard RNNs and many SSMs are effectively first-order: the current state depends only on the immediate predecessor. Here, y_i may depend on multiple previous outputs, yielding higher-order recurrence. The motivation is straightforward: forcing all history through a single-step state update can bottleneck expressivity, while allowing multi-step dependence may recover richer memory behavior without paying full quadratic attention cost.

Third, the authors construct families of mixers by imposing structure on A and B. Different sparsity patterns and recurrence structures yield different complexity classes, from linear to near-linear, subquadratic, and quadratic. The intended message is that there is a broad middle ground between cheap but restrictive first-order recurrence and fully expressive but expensive dense attention.

Fourth, the framework supports both recurrent execution and parallel-solver views. Since Y = (I-B)^{-1}AX, one can exploit matrix structure for more parallel training-time computation instead of relying purely on token-by-token recurrence. That matters because many recurrence-based alternatives are attractive at inference but weak in training parallelism; the paper argues that structured B can soften that trade-off.

Relative to prior work, this is less a single new module than a unifying algebraic view plus a systematic exploration of higher-order recurrence inside that view.33:T6f3,The experiments are split between synthetic tasks and language-model pretraining. The synthetic side is mainly for mechanism validation: it tests long-range dependency handling, memory propagation, and the effect of recurrence order. The key qualitative result is that higher-order recurrence improves tasks that require information to propagate across multiple steps, suggesting that the added recurrence order buys real modeling capacity rather than only formal flexibility.

The language-model side uses small-to-medium pretraining setups to compare perplexity and efficiency across mixer designs. The emphasis is not on leaderboard-style claims, but on tracing a continuous performance/complexity frontier. Linear-complexity designs are cheapest but more limited; O(n log n) and O(n^{3/2}) constructions recover part of the gap toward attention; full quadratic designs remain the most flexible but also the most expensive. That empirical shape is central to the paper’s argument.

The most useful results are likely the ablations: changing recurrence order, bandwidth, sparsity pattern in B, and direct-connectivity structure in A, then measuring how quality and cost move. For architecture researchers, those ablations are more informative than the final headline numbers because they map directly to controllable design variables.

At the same time, the paper appears closer to proof-of-concept than to production-scale validation. It does not provide strong evidence that these mixers can replace Transformer attention in large frontier LLM pretraining. If reading with deployment in mind, focus on whether the paper reports training stability, throughput, memory footprint, cache size, and scaling with sequence length; those matter more than a single perplexity point.34:T59a,Start with the framework section and the main figure. The whole paper rests on understanding what A and B mean: A captures direct input-to-output influence, while B captures recurrent propagation through previous outputs. Once that is clear, attention, SSMs, and higher-order recurrences all fit into one picture.

Next, read the sections that map existing architectures into this framework. The important part is not the algebra itself, but how the authors use A/B structure to explain cache size, parallelism, and long-range capacity. Two useful questions while reading: why can attention express global dependencies with B = 0, and what changes when dependency is shifted into B?

Then read the complexity-design section carefully. Focus on how the O(n), O(n log n), O(n^{3/2}), and O(n^2) constructions are obtained, and which sparsity or recurrence patterns make them possible. The main thing to probe is whether these structures are only mathematically neat or also hardware-friendly.

In the experiments, prioritize the ablations over the final summary table. If implementation potential matters, spend additional time on the appendices covering solver details, complexity arguments, and exact structural definitions.35:T8c0,方法核心是 learnable block experts routing。作者的出发点有两个观察。第一，原始 token-level router 产生的 expert scores 本身已经包含了专家重要性信息，不一定需要重新设计一套完全不同的路由器。第二，不同 denoising step、不同 block 的专家分布集中度差异很大，因此压缩 unique experts 不能用固定阈值硬裁。

具体做法是先从 token-level expert scores 出发，聚合成 block-level expert scores。直观上，就是把一个 block 内多个 token 对各专家的偏好汇总，得到“这一整个 block 更值得保留哪些专家”的全局排序。然后再用这些 block-level scores 去约束原始 token-level routing：每个 token 仍然保留原来的 top-k 选择机制，但候选专家集合会被 block-level 结果裁剪，只允许在一个较小的共享专家池中选择。这样做的关键点是，它压缩的是一个前向步内的 unique expert count，而不是减少每个 token 的 active experts 数量，因此理论上更容易保住模型表达能力。

作者进一步引入 top-p 形式的动态控制，而不是固定保留前 m 个 block experts。原因是不同 denoising step 的路由熵不同：有些 step 专家偏好很集中，可以压得更狠；有些 step 更分散，需要保留更多候选。top-p 让保留的专家数随 block-level score 分布自适应变化。

训练上采用 self-distillation。论文描述是，在 forward pass 中就使用与推理一致的 routing procedure，让模型在受限专家集合下学习恢复原模型行为。这一点很重要，因为如果只在推理时硬套 block-level 约束，分布偏移会更明显。自蒸馏的作用是把原始 token-level 路由下的能力尽量迁移到压缩后的执行路径上。

从方法定位看，dMoE 不是改 MoE 层结构，也不是做 expert merging / pruning 的离线压缩，而是一个运行时可调的 routing compression 机制。它与 EC-DLM、TEAM、DES 的区别在于：它直接针对“单步 unique experts 过多”这个 dLLM 特有瓶颈，用 block 级共享候选池来压缩激活集合，而不是主要从负载均衡、跨 step 复用或候选约束的其他角度切入。36:T95c,The core idea is a learnable block-level routing mechanism for MoE diffusion LLMs. The method is motivated by two observations. First, the original token-level router scores already contain useful information about expert importance, so one does not need to redesign routing from scratch. Second, expert concentration varies substantially across denoising steps and across blocks, so a fixed compression rule is too rigid.

Concretely, dMoE starts from token-level expert scores and aggregates them into block-level expert scores. Intuitively, it summarizes how strongly the tokens in a block collectively prefer each expert, producing a block-wise ranking over experts. These block-level scores are then used to constrain the original token-level routing. Each token still keeps its original top-k routing behavior, but the candidate expert set is restricted to a smaller shared pool selected at the block level. This is the key design choice: dMoE compresses the number of unique experts activated in one forward pass, rather than reducing the number of active experts per token. That makes it easier to preserve expressivity while improving efficiency.

The method further uses a top-p style dynamic control instead of keeping a fixed number of block experts. The reason is that routing entropy changes across denoising steps: some steps have highly concentrated expert preferences and can be compressed aggressively, while others require a broader candidate set. Top-p allows the number of retained experts to adapt to the score distribution.

Training uses self-distillation. The paper states that the same routing procedure is applied in the forward pass during training, so the model learns to operate under the compressed expert set rather than only facing that constraint at inference time. This matters because otherwise the routing restriction would introduce a larger train-test mismatch. Self-distillation helps transfer the behavior of the original token-level routing into the compressed execution path.

Positionally, dMoE is not an MoE-layer redesign and not an offline pruning or merging method. It is a runtime-adjustable routing compression mechanism. Compared with prior efficient MoE methods for diffusion LMs such as EC-DLM, TEAM, and DES, its focus is more direct: reduce the unique expert set within each denoising step by introducing a block-level shared candidate pool.37:T672,The base model is LLaDA2.0-mini, evaluated on MATH500, GSM8K, ARC-C, and MMLU. The headline numbers are fairly concrete: dMoE reduces the number of uniquely activated experts by 4.77x on average while retaining 99.11% of the original performance, cuts memory usage by 76.64% to 79.84%, and delivers 1.14x to 1.66x end-to-end latency speedup. These are meaningful numbers because such memory and latency gains would be hard to obtain if expert activation were only reduced marginally.

The most important experimental view is the efficiency-quality curve rather than any single benchmark score. The paper emphasizes that dMoE is tunable, meaning the compression level can be adjusted through top-p to fit different deployment constraints. If the full paper includes such curves, the key question is where quality starts to degrade noticeably as unique experts are compressed. That boundary reveals how much representational flexibility is lost when routing is forced into a shared block-level candidate pool.

Another critical part is latency profiling. The introduction says Section 3 shows that MoE latency scales linearly with the number of unique experts and dominates end-to-end inference. That profiling is the foundation of the paper. If it is done carefully, then dMoE is not just an empirical trick but a direct intervention on the actual bottleneck.

It is also important to inspect comparisons against prior efficient MoE methods for diffusion LMs, including EC-DLM, TEAM, and DES. The paper claims a better performance-efficiency trade-off, but that claim should be checked under matched base models, decoding settings, and expert budgets.38:T578,This is worth more than a quick skim if you care about diffusion LMs or sparse scaling. Start with the first half of the introduction and make sure the bottleneck is convincing: block-parallel denoising amplifies the unique-expert problem under token-level routing. In the method section, focus on three questions. First, how exactly are block-level expert scores aggregated from token-level scores? If you are tracking diffusion LM architecture choices, this is more useful than a generic efficiency patch.39:Tb25,方法名是 CoFRe，对应一整套从架构到训练再到推理的设计。

第一部分是 FP-MGM，也就是 fixed-point masked generative model。作者把原始 masked denoiser 中间的一部分 Transformer 层替换成一个共享参数的 fixed-point block。这个 block 会被重复应用若干次，直到达到某种平衡态，平衡态表示作为该层输出。这样做有两个直接效果：一是参数量下降，因为多层显式堆叠变成了同一模块反复使用；二是有效深度不再固定，可以通过 solver iteration 数控制。作者把这个思路分别实例化到文本 MDLM 和图像 MaskGIT 上，得到 FP-MDLM 和 FP-MaskGIT。

第二部分是 cross-step consistency loss，记作 L_CONS。作者认为仅仅把层改成 fixed-point 还不够，因为 masked generation 的相邻去噪步之间，输入 token 会发生离散跳变：有些位置从 mask 变成可见 token，有些位置保持 mask，有些位置保持已知 token。这会让表示空间也出现不连续变化，尤其在低预算采样时更明显。为此，论文引入一个跨步一致性损失，让较噪的 student state 在表示上对齐较干净的 teacher state。文中把它解释为一种 cross-time self-distillation。它的作用不是直接改变 sampler，而是让 denoiser 学到更平滑的时间演化，从而在较少 refinement step 或较少 block forward pass 时仍能给出更稳的 masked-token 预测。

第三部分是 three-state reuse（3SR）。固定点模型常见的提速方法是 warm-start：用上一步的 fixed-point 解作为下一步求解初值。但在 MGM 里，上一时刻的解并不是对所有 token 都同样可信，因为 token 状态变了。作者把位置分成三类：未变化且可见的 token，仍然被 mask 的 token，以及新揭示出来的 token。3SR 对这三类位置采用不同的复用强度：对未变化可见 token 几乎完全复用上一步解；对仍 mask 的位置部分复用；对新揭示 token 更依赖当前输入注入。这个设计很贴合 masked generation 的离散状态机，而不是把 DEQ 的 warm-start 机械照搬过来。

第四部分是 checkpoint conversion。作者还展示了一个实用路径：已有的 MDLM checkpoint 不必从头重训，可以通过一个较短的蒸馏阶段转成 FP-MDLM。这一点对研究和工程都重要，因为它降低了验证 fixed-point 架构的试验成本。

和已有方法相比，这篇的区别在于：它不是单纯改 reveal schedule，也不是做 token skipping 或 mask-aware sparse compute，而是把“每一步 denoiser 的深度是否应该固定”作为核心问题来处理；同时它明确指出，离散 masked generation 需要额外的跨步表示约束和状态感知复用，否则 fixed-point 结构本身并不能自动带来低预算优势。3a:Ta04,The full method is called CoFRe and combines architecture, training loss, and inference-time reuse.

First, the paper introduces FP-MGMs. The middle part of the masked denoiser is replaced with a shared fixed-point block. Instead of stacking many distinct transformer layers, the model repeatedly applies the same block and uses the equilibrium representation as the output. This reduces parameters and allows the effective depth to be controlled by the number of solver iterations. The idea is instantiated for text with MDLM, producing FP-MDLM, and for images with MaskGIT, producing FP-MaskGIT.

Second, the paper adds a cross-step consistency loss, L_CONS. The motivation is that masked generation has abrupt discrete changes between neighboring denoising steps: some positions stay visible, some remain masked, and some become newly revealed. These abrupt token-state changes induce non-smooth hidden-state transitions, which are especially harmful under low sampling budgets. L_CONS aligns the representation of a noisier student state with that of a cleaner teacher state. The paper frames this as a form of cross-time self-distillation. Its role is to make the denoiser’s temporal evolution smoother and to sharpen masked-token predictions when only limited compute is available.

Third, the paper proposes three-state reuse (3SR) for warm-starting the fixed-point solver. Standard fixed-point models often initialize the next solve from the previous equilibrium. In masked generation, that previous solution is not equally trustworthy for all token positions because the token states have changed. 3SR therefore treats three token categories differently: unchanged visible tokens, still-masked tokens, and newly revealed tokens. Unchanged visible tokens reuse the previous solution strongly, still-masked tokens reuse it partially, and newly revealed tokens rely more on the current input injection. This is a masked-generation-specific adaptation of warm-starting rather than a direct import from DEQ models.

Finally, the paper shows that pretrained MDLM checkpoints can be converted into FP-MDLMs through a short distillation stage, avoiding full retraining. That makes the approach more practical for research iteration.

Relative to prior work, the key distinction is that the paper does not mainly optimize the reveal schedule or skip masked-token computation. It asks whether denoiser depth itself should remain fixed across refinement steps, and answers that with a shared fixed-point denoiser plus temporal regularization and state-aware reuse.3b:T747,The paper reports several concrete gains. On OpenWebText, FP-MDLM reduces parameter count by 38.8%, training time by 11.5%, and VRAM usage by 16.9% relative to the baseline MDLM. Under low-budget generation, at budget 96, generative perplexity improves from 830.8 to 375.6. That already shows a much better quality-cost trade-off from the fixed-point denoiser alone. With cross-step consistency and 3SR added, the full CoFRe system further improves over MDLM+SDTT in the low-budget regime; the excerpt indicates additional gains but does not preserve the full final number.

The same framework is also applied to MaskGIT on ImageNette, which is important because it shows the method is not text-only. Even though the provided excerpt does not include the full image-side tables, the paper’s framing is clearly multimodal: fixed-point masked denoisers are presented as a general MGM efficiency mechanism.

The most informative ablations are along three axes. First, architecture ablations show that fixed-point replacement alone cuts parameters, time, and memory while improving low-budget generation. Second, objective ablations indicate that L_CONS is the main driver of low-budget gains; the authors explicitly state that it accounts for most of the improvement. Third, inference ablations show that 3SR is what makes warm-starting viable under discrete token-state transitions. Another practical result is checkpoint conversion: a pretrained MDLM can be distilled into an FP-MDLM without full retraining.

DLLM-JEPA 的关键构造是：从同一个输入采样两个噪声级别 tL < tH，形成两个 view。
- context view x_{tL}：低噪声，保留大部分 token；
- target view x_{tH}：高噪声，信息更残缺。

模型对 context view 做一次带梯度前向，得到两类输出：
1. diffusion logits，用于标准 masked denoising loss；
2. pooled embedding z_{tL}，作为 JEPA 的预测端表示。

对 target view 再做一次无梯度前向，得到目标 embedding z_{tH}。随后用 JEPA loss 让 context-side 表示去预测 target-side 表示。因为 target 分支 stop-gradient，所以每步只有一次带梯度前向，而不是像 LLM-JEPA 那样两路都反传；这就是 33% FLOPs 节省的来源。

从设计取舍看，这个方案有几个值得注意的点：
1. 为什么用不同 mask rate 作为两视角，而不是随机 span corruption 或外部数据增强？因为 diffusion schedule 已经定义了语义一致、信息量不同的 view family，天然适合做“同一语义、不同可见度”的预测；
2. 为什么 target 分支不回传梯度？这是 JEPA/Bootstrap 类方法常见做法，用来稳定训练并减少计算；
3. 为什么作者强调与 LLM-JEPA 不是直接 apples-to-apples 比较？因为一个建立在 AR block-causal attention 上，一个建立在 bidirectional masked diffusion 上，结构约束不同，直接横比容易把架构差异和目标函数差异混在一起。

论文还分析了表示层面的变化。作者发现加入 DLLM-JEPA 后，隐藏态相对预训练模型的 drift 更大，尤其集中在中间层，但 Wikitext 上的功能性遗忘更小。这说明 JEPA 不是简单地做“靠近原模型”的正则，而是在重塑中层组合结构表示，使模型在任务适配和基础能力保持之间取得更好的平衡。作者还做了 collapse 检查，说明 embedding 预测没有退化成平凡常数表示。3e:T558,Its significance for pretraining research is not that it proves diffusion LMs will replace AR models. In vision, JEPA avoids low-level reconstruction bias by predicting latent representations rather than pixels. This paper shows that masked diffusion LMs are structurally better suited than AR LMs for that idea.

Three takeaways matter. First, the diffusion noise level itself can serve as a view generator, so language JEPA does not need externally paired data. But if diffusion LMs continue to mature, latent prediction objectives like this could become an important recipe component.3f:T97d,The method is built on masked diffusion LMs such as LLaDA. Starting from a clean sequence x0, the forward process replaces each token with [MASK] independently with probability t, and the model learns to reconstruct the original tokens from the masked sequence xt. Unlike AR models, the backbone uses bidirectional attention, so one forward pass already yields a full-context representation.

DLLM-JEPA constructs two views from the same input by sampling two noise levels tL < tH:
- a context view x_{tL}, lightly masked and information-rich;
- a target view x_{tH}, heavily masked and more abstract.

A gradient-carrying forward pass is run on the context view. From that pass, the model produces:
1. diffusion logits for the standard denoising loss;
2. a pooled embedding z_{tL}, used as the JEPA prediction-side representation.

The target view is processed in a second forward pass without gradient, producing z_{tH}. A JEPA loss then trains the context-side representation to predict the target-side representation. Because the target branch is stop-gradient, only one branch backpropagates each step. That is the source of the reported 33% FLOP reduction relative to LLM-JEPA.

Several design choices are worth noting. Using different mask rates as the two views is more principled than ad hoc text augmentation because the diffusion schedule already defines a family of semantically aligned but information-varying views. Keeping the target branch gradient-free follows the usual JEPA/bootstrap logic for stability and efficiency. The paper also avoids a direct head-to-head comparison with LLM-JEPA as if they were identical settings, since one lives on block-causal AR attention and the other on bidirectional masked diffusion; otherwise architecture effects and objective effects would be entangled.

A particularly interesting part is the representation analysis. DLLM-JEPA increases hidden-state drift from the pretrained model, especially in middle transformer layers, yet reduces functional forgetting measured on Wikitext. That suggests JEPA is not acting like a simple stay-close-to-initialization regularizer. Instead, it appears to redirect adaptation toward more useful internal structure, especially in the middle layers often associated with compositional processing. The paper also checks for representation collapse and reports that the JEPA objective does not degenerate into trivial constant embeddings.40:T6d5,The experiments cover four tasks and two diffusion backbones, with diffusion-only fine-tuning on the same backbone as the main baseline. Empirically, it fixes the model and target sequence in LLaDA-2.1-mini, varies only the reveal order, and evaluates the pathwise conditional probabilities q_t(π)=pθ(x*_{π(t)}|R_{t-1},c). If these conditionals came from a coherent joint distribution, the chain rule would make the sum of log q_t invariant to order. The paper shows that this invariance fails in practice.

The theoretical contribution is the uniform-spreading theorem. The authors frame target recovery as a sequence of local argmax decisions. At each step, success depends not only on the target probability q_t itself, but on whether it wins against local competitors. Holding the total budget P=∏t q_t fixed, recoverability is uniquely maximized when confidence is spread uniformly across steps, q_t=P^(1/n). The structural penalty for uneven allocation is captured by Var(log q_t). This yields two complementary diagnostics: logP measures total confidence budget, while Var(log q_t) measures how efficiently a reveal order distributes that budget.

The paper then analyzes several decoding strategies: Forced-AR, Random, and confidence-first variants such as Max-prob and Top-margin. A notable empirical finding is that confidence-first decoding, although order-agnostic in principle, follows reveal paths that are close to left-to-right on content tokens. Its main deviation appears in short-answer settings, where it can trigger a tail-EOS cascade.43:T5d7,The main experiments use LLaDA-2.1-mini on fixed target continuations from C4. The authors sample 1,000 random C4 examples, split each into a prefix and target continuation, and compare path scores under different reveal orders. The headline result is that changing only the order can shift logP/n by as much as 0.49 nats per token. That is far beyond numerical noise and is strong evidence that the learned conditionals are not exact factorizations of one coherent joint distribution.

For generation behavior, the paper compares one-token-per-step strategies. Structured strategies—Forced-AR, Max-prob, and Top-margin—show similar external perplexity, but substantially lower Var(log q_t) than Random. Reveal-order analysis explains why: Max-prob and Top-margin traverse content-token paths that are very close to strict left-to-right decoding, so their behavior is much less exotic than the order-agnostic label suggests. The main difference comes from short-answer prompts, where confidence-first rules can exploit a tail-EOS cascade.

Downstream validation covers HellaSwag, CMath, MMLU-Pro, and IFEval. The point is not headline benchmark gains, but the relationship between correctness and the variance axis. Lower Var(log q_t) is consistently associated with correct generations, and the pattern is not reducible to Random simply being weak overall. The natural follow-up questions are whether training can explicitly enforce path consistency, and whether the observed 0.49 nats/token order drift shrinks or grows at larger dLLM scales.45:T689,DAG-MoE replaces the standard weighted-sum aggregation with a learned directed acyclic graph over the selected top-K experts. Routing remains unchanged: a conventional sparse router picks the top-K experts for each token. The new part is a lightweight DAG-learning module that assigns structural roles to those K experts and aggregates them through iterative updates along the learned graph.

The motivation is straightforward. Weighted summation cannot express ordered compositions such as “expert A processes first, expert B refines based on A.” It also lacks intermediate states, since every expert output is projected directly into the final mixture. By introducing a DAG, the model can form short computation chains inside a single MoE layer, where some expert outputs become intermediate nodes consumed by later experts.

The theoretical argument is that, with experts and router fixed, structural aggregation enlarges the effective combination space. The same set of selected experts can now realize different functions depending on graph structure, whereas weighted sum collapses all permutations into one. The paper further argues that this enables a form of approximate multi-step reasoning within one layer, especially for compositional problems such as dynamic-programming-like computations.

Implementation-wise, the design is intentionally local. The graph is learned only among the selected K experts, not over all N experts. This keeps the extra cost tied to K rather than to the full expert pool. That design choice is central: the paper is not trying to replace sparse routing, but to replace the overly simple aggregation that follows sparse routing.46:T60b,The experiments cover language modeling and downstream tasks, and the consistent message is that DAG-MoE improves over standard MoE when the router and expert backbone are otherwise kept comparable. The key claim is not a single headline number, but that changing only the aggregation mechanism can produce gains under the same expert-selection setup.

The most informative part is the ablation section. Several takeaways matter:
1. DAG aggregation still helps when expert granularity cannot be pushed further or when routing overhead is already a bottleneck, suggesting it is a genuinely different scaling axis.
2. Compared with simply increasing expert count, active experts, or FFN depth, structural aggregation appears to offer a better trade-off under controlled routing complexity.
3. Removing DAG learning or replacing it with unstructured/fixed aggregation degrades performance, which suggests the gain is not merely from extra computation steps but from learned inter-expert dependencies.
4. The advantage is more visible on tasks with stronger compositional structure, which is aligned with the paper’s “single-layer multi-step reasoning” argument.

When reading, it is important to verify whether FLOPs, active experts, and hidden sizes are tightly matched; otherwise the improvement could partly come from extra effective compute rather than aggregation alone.47:T42f,Resonant Context Anchoring (RCA) explicitly decouples two roles of self-attention:
- Routing: which tokens are selected (governed by attention probabilities).
- Gain: how strongly selected information impacts the residual stream (governed by the magnitude of the Value vectors).

RCA uses raw pre-softmax attention scores (QK^T) as an instantaneous semantic-correlation (“resonance”) signal. When a query strongly correlates with certain context tokens, RCA amplifies the norms of the corresponding Value vectors via a gated nonlinearity. Crucially, it does not modify the attention probability distribution, aiming to preserve syntactic structure and general fluency while increasing the contextual subspace energy relative to parametric components injected by MLPs.

Compared to prior inference-time methods:
- Versus contrastive decoding: no multiple forward passes; negligible latency overhead.
- Versus activation/head suppression: it boosts contextual evidence instead of bluntly suppressing parametric memory, reducing the risk of harming coherence/perplexity.48:Ta7d,技术路线分成三步，逻辑很完整。

第一步是把 locate-then-edit 框架尽量原样迁移到 MDM。作者比较了两类 AR 模型（LLaMA、Qwen）和两类 MDM（LLaDA、Dream），并尽量做 matched scale 对比。方法基础仍然沿用 ROME / MEMIT 的解释：Transformer MLP 的 down-projection 矩阵可视为线性关联记忆，last subject token 处的 up-projection activation 作为 key，value 编码 relation-object 信息；编辑就是在选定层的 MLP 权重上加入低秩或解析更新，使同一个 key 映射到新的 object 表征。对 MDM 的改动只限于适配 masked prediction，而不是重写编辑算法，这样实验结论更能回答“原有假设是否成立”。

第二步是做 causal tracing 和 edit-site sweep，区分“知识位置”和“编辑成效”两个问题。作者先用 causal tracing 看事实回忆对哪些层、哪些 token 位置最敏感，再系统扫描不同 token position 和 layer range 上的编辑效果。结果显示，即便 MDM 是双向建模、所有 token 都能看完整 subject，事实回忆最关键的位置仍然是 early-to-mid layer 的 last subject token MLP。这一点很关键，因为它说明 locate-then-edit 的位置假设并不是 AR 专属产物，而更像是 Transformer 在实体-关系检索上的一个稳定机制。

第三步是诊断并修复 MDM 的 multi-token breakdown。作者发现单 token target object 上，MDM 和 ARM 的编辑效果接近；但一旦目标 object 跨多个 token，MDM 性能明显下降。论文给出的解释很有说服力：标准 locate-then-edit 只在一个“理想状态”上拟合编辑，也就是模型在预测目标 token 时的某个内部表示。AR 解码是左到右的，生成时会自然经过这个被拟合的状态，所以编辑能生效。MDM 则从 fully masked 输出开始，经过多轮去噪，依次经历一系列不同的 partial-mask states；原始编辑更新没有针对这些中间状态做鲁棒化，因此多 token object 的后续 token 会在不匹配的状态分布下被生成，导致编辑逐步失效。

为了解决这个问题，作者提出一个简单修正：让编辑更新对去噪过程中的中间 partial-mask states 也保持有效。全文摘要没有给出全部公式细节，但从描述看，核心不是换新的编辑位点，而是在构造目标 value / 优化约束时，把多种 mask 状态纳入编辑拟合，使同一事实更新在不同去噪阶段都能维持一致方向。这个修正的价值在于，它直接对应了 MDM 与 ARM 的生成机制差异，而不是把失败归因于“MDM 不适合知识编辑”这种过宽泛的结论。49:T431,This matters for pretraining research in three ways. First, it adds a useful mechanistic result for non-AR language modeling: at least for factual recall, MDMs appear to use a memory localization pattern similar to AR transformers, which suggests that the common interpretation of MLPs as associative memory is not tied to next-token training alone. First, the authors transfer locate-then-edit to MDMs with minimal changes. They compare two AR models (LLaMA and Qwen) and two MDMs (LLaDA and Dream) at matched scale. The underlying editing view remains the same as in ROME and MEMIT: the MLP down-projection is treated as a linear associative memory, the up-projection activation at the last subject token serves as the key, and the value encodes relation-object information. Editing modifies the selected MLP weights so that the same key maps to a new target object representation. For MDMs, the algorithm is adapted only as needed for masked prediction, not redesigned from scratch. This is important because it allows the paper to test whether the original assumptions survive the paradigm shift.

Second, the paper disentangles localization from effectiveness. It uses causal tracing to identify which token positions and layers are causally responsible for factual recall, and then performs systematic sweeps over edit positions and layer ranges. The main result is strikingly consistent: even though MDMs are bidirectional and every token can attend to the full subject, factual recall still concentrates in the early-to-mid-layer MLPs at the last subject token, just as in AR models. That means the canonical edit site from AR knowledge editing is not merely an artifact of left-to-right training.

Third, the paper diagnoses and repairs the multi-token failure mode in MDMs. For single-token target objects, editing performance is comparable between ARMs and MDMs. But as the target object spans more tokens, MDM performance drops sharply. The explanation is tied to generation dynamics. Standard locate-then-edit fits the update at a single internal state. In an AR model, left-to-right decoding naturally passes through that fitted state when generating the edited token sequence. In an MDM, generation starts from a fully masked output and proceeds through multiple denoising steps, traversing a chain of partial-mask states that the edit was never optimized for. As a result, later tokens in a multi-token object are generated under mismatched internal conditions, and the edit degrades.

To address this, the authors propose a simple correction that makes the edit robust to those intermediate partial-mask states. The excerpt does not expose every formula, but the conceptual move is clear: instead of fitting the edit to a single idealized state, the update is constrained to remain effective across the family of states encountered during denoising. The value of this fix is that it directly targets the generative mismatch between AR and MDM inference, rather than attributing the failure to a vague claim that diffusion-style LMs are hard to edit.4b:T733,The experiments are organized around two questions: whether factual localization transfers, and why editing quality diverges.
